items.item: graduateManual is an unauthenticated trigger (no privilege, no creator signature)
items.subItem: Premature finalization before graduation window open; timing front-run
items.status: NO CONFIRMED PERMISSIONLESS PROFIT PATH (main trigger decided); residual open
items.exactBlocker: All 7 live Manual curves have graduation_time in the past; no fixture with an open window exists on mainnet.
items.nextAction: Find or archive a live Manual curve whose launch window is still open; execute graduateManual before graduationTime has passed; measure whether the trigger succeeds and whether the caller gains anything.
items.notes: The main trigger is decided: any wallet can finalize a past-window Manual curve; everything moved is bound to the curve record. The only open questions are (a) whether it also fires before the window closes, and (b) the timing/front-run implication (any wallet may choose the finalization moment). Neither affects the permissionless-profit conclusion.

No Whirlpool pool exists for the largest pre-graduation WSOL curves, so attacker-submitted variants terminate on 6022/6023 account checks rather than authorization decisions.

Replay with exact account list; test substitution of Whirlpool pool, position, escrow, token badges, fee accounts, and vault binding. Do not substitute missing accounts.

Executed attempts hit seed check (6023) for non-existent escrow; LpTakeover reaches privilege gate (6027, privilege 11).

items.requiredSigner: LpTakeover requires privilege 11 (AuthorityConfig). LpHarvest requires ownership of the position (position-bound).
items.nextAction: If an exact historical pre-state with a funded lp_escrow becomes available (indexer/archive), replay with the real escrow and position. Test harvest without owning position, position/escrow substitution, LP mint substitution, pool/vault substitution, recipient/rewarder substitution, zero/underfunded escrow, repeated harvest, transfer-then-harvest, harvest-then-transfer, close-then-harvest. items.item: TokenRefund payout arithmetic on genuinely expired, non-graduated curve
items.exactBlocker: Every candidate curve returns 6016 (bonding curve still active) before reaching the refund arithmetic; no genuinely expired, non-graduated curve exists in the live 1,537-curve set.
items.fixture: None — no expired, non-graduated live curve.
items.requiredSigner: No special signer required; the caller must own the position/ATA being refunded.
items.nextAction: Locate an expired, non-graduated curve (requires either a historical fixture or a future time-travel, neither of which is available). Execute TokenRefund against its quote vault; measure the arithmetic: quote-vault delta, base-vault delta (if any), refund destination binding, mint binding, token-program pinning, protocol-vault delta, attacker delta. Test repeated refund, refund followed by sell/withdraw/close, and the reverse sequence. Record the exact arithmetic (not just the gate).
items.notes: The gate (6016) is enforced; that is decided. The arithmetic (how much the quote vault releases, how the refund destination binds to the stored field, what happens when the stored destination is Pubkey::default()) is unmeasured. Do not claim the arithmetic safe without measuring it.

items.item: Buy path with a genuine provider-signed permission
items.exactBlocker: All 1,537 live curves set buyRequiresPermission = true. Every buy needs a secp256k1 signature from the single configured allowed signer (0359c54abfca..2b29). Without that key the buy-side payout/fee/rounding arithmetic cannot be reached. We deliberately did not forge a consumed-permission account or use cheatcodes.
items.fixture: Cached raw consume->buy pair exists in recon/txs/ (historical live message + signature). The pre-state at the original slot is unavailable (fork moved on before replay).
items.requiredSigner: The allowed signer (0359c54abfca..2b29) — unavailable. The consumer (subject) must match the permission; the curve must match.
items.nextAction: Replay the cached consume->buy pair verbatim at its exact pre-state (restore from recon/txs/ and from the original transaction meta). Then mutate one field at a time: subject, consumer, amount, mint, curve, quote vault, destination, expiry, signature, consumed-PDA derivation, token program, remaining accounts. Then test combinations: consume->buy, consume->buy->sell, consume->buy->refund, consume->buy->transfer, repeated consume->buy, two buys using one permission, buy using a permission consumed for another subject/curve/amount. Verify signature domain separation, consumed-PDA derivation, amount binding, expiry, subject binding, actual vault balance movement. Without a genuine signed fixture, the arithmetic path remains INCOMPLETE.
items.notes: The permission gate and binding checks are decided (6018, 6001, 6004, 6003, 6002, 6023, 6024, 6025). What remains open is the arithmetic: does the buy path correctly compute the quote amount, apply fees, and move tokens? That requires a genuine signed message to reach the arithmetic code.

items.item: Legitimate funded deposit -> swap -> withdraw -> close accounting
items.exactBlocker: MarketInitialize with the correct 10-account shape and an attacker-chosen market id terminates with 'Account <attacker> is not the authority' (IncorrectAuthority, error 1). Market creation is gated to the hardcoded initializer (CGYAxnDF1bYwmbzTtVx2pdo8xd3aviqE58WumVYRLYRH, rodata 0x38a48). No market-authority key is available; no genuine deposit/withdraw/close fixture exists in recon/s4_bb_sigs.json.
items.fixture: No self-owned market possible; no genuine market lifecycle fixture available from the 32 live markets' transaction histories (recon/s4_bb_sigs.json shows authority-updater transactions, not attacker-owned lifecycle).
items.requiredSigner: Market authority (hardcoded initializer CGYAxnDF… or per-market authority from the 12-authority set) — unavailable.
items.nextAction: Replay a genuine market lifecycle from the market PDA's own transaction history at pre-state (replayOf from recon/s4_bb_sigs.json). Test account/recipient/vault substitution; measure protocol loss separately from ordinary arbitrage; verify reserve/accounting conservation. If no such fixture exists, document the limitation explicitly in the final report.
items.notes: We deliberately did not call owner/restricted functions or use cheatcodes to fabricate a market-authority state. The authority gate (IncorrectAuthority) is measured and decided. The accounting (how reserves, vaults, and fees move through a full lifecycle) is unmeasured.

items.item: Penalty selection (arbPenaltyPerM / cuPenaltyMultiplier / jitodFrontPenaltyPerM) — can penalties be avoided rather than paid?
items.status: INCOMPLETE (economic measurement decided; arithmetic control open)
items.exactBlocker: Every accepted fill's effective price is consistent with the configured arbPenaltyPerM being applied (300 on 28 markets, 0 on 4 frozen-window markets). cuPenaltyMultiplier = 0 everywhere. Whether penalties can be dodged (rather than paid) requires controlling the oracle push — i.e., a market updater key (BP8TxUroBDw97JWmc9bfg9bs8PoE6MA71SSihhBNUJR4 on 22 markets, plus 8 per-market updater keys). No updater fixture exists; we neither called owner/restricted functions nor impersonated an updater.
items.fixture: Live market state (32 markets, 14 funded, 18 zero-reserve) — available. Updater-signed OracleUpdate payload — unavailable.
items.requiredSigner: Market updater (BP8TxUro… or per-market updater) — unavailable.
items.nextAction: Obtain an updater-signed OracleUpdate payload; test whether a permissionless swap can suppress or bypass the configured penalties by providing a custom oracle payload. Without the updater key, the arithmetic control path remains INCOMPLETE; the economic measurement (every accepted fill priced consistently with penalties applied) stays valid and is documented in BBS2_stale_sweep.json and BUSYBOX_DEEP_REVIEW.md §5.2.
items.notes: This is the only remaining open item for Busybox that relates to a genuine arithmetic question (not just a missing fixture). The economic measurement is authoritative: 139 probes, both directions, three sizes, same-slot external reference, every round trip negative, max positive +11.06 USD (0.39% of a $2,892 leg), sum of positives $19.01 — no exploitable profit path. The open question is whether penalties can be dodged; that requires updater control.

The previous record (FINAL_DISPOSITION.md §4.5, BUSYBOX_DEEP_REVIEW.md §3) claimed the opposite; that claim came from comparing the last oracle update slot (not `slot > validUntil`).
